content_sections.title: Learn the management sense of run
content_sections.body_text: Here run means manage or organize an activity, service, or organization. ‘Lan runs a language club.’ ‘They run a weekend course.’ Identify what is managed after run, then create one true or invented example about a club, event, service, course, or business.

content_sections.title: Place management before a past point
content_sections.body_text: ‘Before the guests arrived, Lan had run several events.’ Had run marks the organizing experience as earlier than arrived. Draw HAD RUN → GUESTS ARRIVED → now. Keep the management meaning by naming the event or organization that Lan managed.

content_sections.title: Mark linking boundaries
content_sections.body_text: At a final-consonant + initial-vowel boundary, move smoothly with no pause or extra vowel: run_an event; event_at school. First say each side, then join it: run|an → run_an, event|at → event_at. Keep /n/ and /t/ audible as they lead into the next vowel.

content_sections.title: Notice, retell, self-check
content_sections.body_text: Model: ‘Before June, Lan had run_an event_at school, so she could organize the club.’ Mark the earlier event, rehearse both linked boundaries, then retell with a different activity. Check: run means manage, had run is earlier than the past reference point, and each marked final consonant remains audible without a pause.
